item.title: Immigration Detention: Changes In Inspections of ICE Facilities Raise Questions About Oversight
item.description:
What GAO Found
Department of Homeland Security (DHS) detention facility inspections have changed at the same time that the number of immigration detention facilities and the size of the detained population have increased. From April 2025 to April 2026, following a January 2025 Executive Order, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) added over 40 detention facilities that detain noncitizens for over 72 hours. The average daily population of detained noncitizens grew by over 50 percent, to 61,817 individuals, over the timeframe. From fiscal year 2024 to July 2026, three of the four DHS entities that conducted inspections changed the frequency (decreased or increased) or stopped conducting inspections.
Changes to Inspections Conducted by DHS Entities from Fiscal Year (FY) 2024 to July 2026
ICE relies on these inspections to identify deficiencies in its facilities and ensure compliance with its detention standards. However, the frequency of inspections has in some cases decreased, there is an increased reliance on self-inspections, and processes for these inspections have changed. ICE has not used evidence, such as data on deficiencies identified through inspections and performance information such as the extent to which facilities are in compliance with their contracts, to determine the effects of these recent changes on facility conditions. By using evidence to determine these effects and applying the results to improve oversight, ICE could ensure that facilities provide sound conditions and care for noncitizens, in accordance with its standards.
Why GAO Did This Study
ICE is authorized to detain noncitizens apprehended for violations of immigration law pending removal proceedings or execution of a removal order. ICE guidance states that ICE must detain noncitizens in the most humane manner possible. ICE has established detention standards that dictate how facilities should operate. ICE relies on various DHS entities within and outside of ICE to assess compliance. These inspections identify deficiencies related to medical care and food service, among other areas.
GAO was asked to review compliance with detention standards and related oversight. This report examines (1) changes to DHS inspections of detention facilities since GAO’s last report on this topic (GAO-25-107580) and (2) ICE's use of evidence to inform its oversight of detention facilities in light of the changes. GAO reviewed documentation on DHS’s various oversight mechanisms and how they changed between fiscal year 2024 and July 2026. GAO also analyzed ICE data on the number of facilities that detain noncitizens for over 72 hours and the average daily population from April 2025 to April 2026. GAO interviewed officials responsible for conducting oversight from various offices within DHS.
